source_title: Feature Detection by Retinal Ganglion Cells.
section: Downstream pathways and behavioral significance of retinal contrast detection.
node_relevance_reason: Names CaMKIIα neurons in vLGN and IGL (innervated by sONα RGCs) projecting to nucleus reuniens with mixed excitation and inhibition.
summary: sONα RGCs innervate CaMKIIα neurons in vLGN and IGL that provide a mixture of excitation and inhibition to nucleus reuniens to promote spatial memory formation (Huang et al. 2021). Distinguished from the GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons projecting to the lateral habenula.
quotes: Second, sONα RGCs innervate CaMKIIα neurons in the vLGN and IGL, which provide a mixture of excitation and inhibition to the nucleus reuniens (Re) to promote spatial memory formation (Huang et al. 2021).
First, sONα RGCs innervate GABAergic neurons in the vLGN and IGL that project to the lateral habenula (LHb) and mediate antidepressant effects of light (Huang et al. 2019).

source_title: Divergent outputs of the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus mediate visually evoked defensive behaviors
node_relevance_reason: Describes a genetically and projection-defined vLGN GABA to nucleus reuniens circuit, with soma in vLGN.
summary: A vLGN to nucleus reuniens circuit is described, distinct from a vLGN to SC circuit, with opposite influence on defensive freezing; vLGN GABA to Re activation increases freezing. Separate vLGN populations project to Re and SC; vLGN GABA to Re activation increases freezing and slows habituation. Re-projecting neurons reside in both external and internal vLGN divisions. Activating vLGN to Re neurons has an effect opposite to activating vLGN to SC neurons; two divergent vLGN GABA output pathways to Re and SC influence freezing oppositely.
quotes: We describe both a vLGN→nucleus reuniens (Re) circuit and a vLGN→superior colliculus (SC) circuit, which exert opposite influences on defensive responses.
Separate populations of vLGN neurons project to the Re versus the SC and exert opposing influences on defensive behaviors to visual threat (Figure 5).
vLGN neurons that target the SC or the Re reside in both divisions and thereby may pool information from visual as well as from non-visual sources.
By contrast, mice with their vLGN GABA →Re neurons activated spent significantly more time freezing and took longer to habituate to looming stimuli.
Our data revealed two divergent vLGN GABA output pathways to the Re and SC, each of which exert opposite influences on freezing behaviors (Figure 5N).

source_title: Enhancement and contextual modulation of visuospatial processing by thalamocollicular projections from ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
node_relevance_reason: Notes inhibitory vLGN projections to nucleus reuniens and Re-dependent promotion of spatial memory, without cell-type markers.
summary: vLGN is predominantly GABAergic and sends long-range inhibitory projections including to nucleus reuniens; vLGN projections to RE promote spatial memory.
quotes: Instead, it sends long-range inhibitory projections to subcortical visual and visuomotor areas in the thalamus and midbrain including the superior colliculus (SC), midbrain reticular nucleus, periaqueductal gray (PAG) and nucleus reuniens (Re) 7,[10][11][12] .

Consistent with this idea, vLGN neurons have been shown to be involved in bright lightdependent anti-depressive and anti-nociceptive effects and promotion of spatial memory via their projections to the lateral habenula, PAG and RE, respectively 11,12,17 .

source_title: Not a one-trick pony: Diverse connectivity and functions of the rodent lateral geniculate complex
node_relevance_reason: Review of vLGN/IGL neurochemistry (mostly GABAergic IGL) with no mention of Re projection or CaMKIIα.
summary: Large fraction of IGL neurons are GABAergic, few glutamatergic; relevant only as background on transmitter identity in the region.
quotes: A large fraction of neurons in IGL generate GABA (Moore & Speh, 1993), few are glutamatergic, and none project axons to visual cortex (Harrington, 1997).
